title: Savings Scorecard and Hypothesis Registry: consolidated initiative-level tracking for batching/caching/quant
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We run many parallel cost-optimization experiments (batching, KV-prefetch/caching, and quantization profiles) without a single canonical way to track hypothesis lifecycles, cross-experiment double-counting, or multi-dimension rollups per model/customer. That makes it hard to attribute savings to initiatives, prioritize experiments, and show clear OKR progress to stakeholders.

Goal: Ship a lightweight initiative-level 'Savings Scorecard' and an accompanying Hypothesis Registry that: 1) registers each experiment/hypothesis with metadata (scope, expected savings range, dependent models/customers), 2) ingests verified experiment results (A/B, canary, field trial) and normalizes savings signals, 3) applies decay/attribution rules to avoid double-counting when multiple knobs (batching + quant) affect the same token stream, and 4) exposes a dashboard and exportable rollups tied to OKRs and release milestones.

Scope: MVP covers batching, KV-cache/prefix caching, and model quantization profiles for hosted and dedicated deployments. Private deployment signals will be supported via a templated CSV ingestion for the initial rollout. The scorecard will surface: cumulative claimed savings, verified realized savings, confidence band, primary attribution (knob), affected model(s), affected customer segments, and link to evaluation artifacts.

Non-goal: This ticket does not implement the experiment automation engine or change runtime behavior. It focuses on the tracking, normalization, and reporting layer plus light integrations to existing signals (cost events, runtime telemetry, and the experiment results store).

Trade-offs discussed: 1) Attribution complexity vs. clarity — we choose a deterministic priority-order attribution (quantization > caching > batching by default) with an override field for critical customers. 2) Real-time vs. batched reconciliation — start with daily reconciliation to avoid noisy instant snapshots. 3) On-chain audit logs vs. aggregated row-level events — aggregate view for dashboard, retention of raw events in the experiment store for forensic work.

Success metrics: 1) Scorecard accepted by Finance and Product (sign-off) as authoritative for Q1 cost OKRs; 2) Reduction in duplicate savings claims by 90% in the first 8 weeks; 3) >70% of active experiments register hypotheses in the registry within 48 hours of kickoff.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Hypothesis Registry UI/API to create/modify hypotheses with required metadata (owner, scope, expected savings, primary knob, start/end dates).
2) Ingestion pipeline from experiment results store that maps experiments to registry entries and computes normalized daily savings per hypothesis.
3) Decay and attribution rules implemented and documented; example cases covered in unit/integration tests.
4) Scorecard dashboard with filters (time range, knob type, model, customer segment) and export to CSV.
5) Stakeholder sign-off from Finance, Product, and Eng on the scorecard numbers for a 2-week pilot dataset.
6) Basic audit trail links back to raw experiment artifacts (PRs, evaluation sets, dashboards).
